triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix formulas let negative inputs propagate — most sharply in `cooperative_reduction`, where a negative QBI allocable to qualified cooperative payments produced a negative 199A(b)(7) 'reduction' that would have increased the deductible amount instead of reducing it — but the statute states no explicit 'but not below zero' floor at any of the four sites, so the clamps may be defensive rather than a source-mismatch repair.
triage.triage_notes: Only modified module in this chunk. Two independent changes: (a) new module-level deferred_outputs for 199A(c), (d) and (h), which is pure metadata (mechanical), and (b) four formulas that wrap operands in max(0, ...): `cooperative_reduction` (199A(b)(7)), `qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi` (199A(a), now max(0, min(combined QBI amount, taxable-income limit))), `cooperative_production_deduction_before_wage_limit` (199A(g)(1)(A)) and `cooperative_production_deduction` (199A(g)(1)(B), clamping W-2 wages). I read 199A through the pinned corpus release: (b)(7) says only 'shall be reduced by the lesser of— (A) 9 percent ... or (B) 50 percent ...' and (g)(1)(A) 'an amount equal to 9 percent of the lesser of— (i) ... or (ii) ...'; neither carries a zero floor, and 199A(c)(1) defines QBI as a 'net amount' that can be negative with (c)(2) handling losses by carryover. So the clamps encode an implied non-negativity rather than quoted text, and the only stated motive in the commit body is the generic 'Repair RuleSpec validation coverage' / 'Repair validation tail for refreshed RuleSpecs' — consistent with a validator-driven clamp. A reviewer should decide whether 'a negative statutory reduction that increases the deduction' counts as a fidelity defect; if kept, `cooperative_reduction` is the strongest single instance because there the sign flip inverts the direction of the adjustment.
triage.verifier_justification: The four changes only wrap already-existing operands in `max(0, ...)`, and the pinned source text has no floor to represent: "but not below zero" occurs zero times in the resolved 26 USC 199A text (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, body sha256 0af6c1cc…), and the one relevant "(if any)" — 199A(a)(2)'s "20 percent of the excess (if any)" — was already encoded pre-fix as `qbi_deduction_rate * max(0, taxable_income_computed_without_section_199A - net_capital_gain)`, untouched by this diff. Three of the four clamped quantities are non-negative by construction or by their own definition (W-2 wages under 199A(b)(4)/6051(a); QPAI is "the excess (if any)" under 199A(g)(3)(A)), so those clamps are no-ops, and the one substantive case — negative QBI allocable to cooperative payments in (b)(7) — is not handled by a statutory floor at all: 199A(c)(2) routes a negative net QBI to a succeeding-year loss carryover, which `max(0, ...)` does not encode. The apply manifest records a hand repair on top of the unchanged generated encoding (`"model": "manual-repair-v1"`, `"tool": "axiom-encode deterministic/manual repair"`, generated_output_sha256 unchanged), and axiom-encode at that exact commit (c0bc4a92) ships a house convention for exactly this shape — `repair-nonnegative-floors` / "Benefit, allotment, credit, deduction, allowance, and subsidy outputs must use `max(0, ...)` before downstream minimums or eligibility branches" — i.e. defensive hardening, not a source-mismatch repair.
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation of the first reader's "unclear / missing_nonnegativity_floor": (1) Source check via the pinned release resolver — 199A(b)(7) reads "shall be reduced by the lesser of— (A) 9 percent ... or (B) 50 percent ..." with no "but not below zero"; 199A(g)(1)(A) reads "9 percent of the lesser of— (i) the qualified production activities income ... or (ii) the taxable income"; 199A(g)(1)(B)(i) "shall not exceed 50 percent of the W-2 wages". No floor clause at any of the four sites. (2) The module already carried unrelated, pre-existing `max(0, ...)` floors (trade_or_business_deductible_amount, trade_or_business_excess_amount, qbi_taxable_income_limit), so the house style predates this commit. (3) The clamped identifiers are unbound external inputs — the module has no `inputs:` block; they appear only inside formulas — so this is input hygiene on values the module does not compute. (4) Encoder-side convention exists and is enforced: src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py at c0bc4a92 defines find_nonnegative_amount_reduction_issues / repair_nonnegative_amount_reductions ("Mechanically floor supported nonnegative amount reduction formulas") and cli.py exposes `repair-nonnegative-floors` (model "nonnegative-floor-v1"). Caveat for the reviewer: that lint's own patterns would NOT match these four formulas (no "-" operator and no identifier containing "max" in the pre-fix expressions; `cooperative_reduction` doesn't even match the benefit/credit/deduction name pattern), so the clamps were hand-applied in the same spirit rather than emitted by that tool. (5) Residual reason a reviewer could keep this as "unclear" rather than "not_a_defect": the (b)(7) pre-fix formula genuinely could return a negative "reduction" that inflates the deduction, and "reduced by" arguably implies a non-negative subtrahend — but that is interpretive, and the statute's actual mechanism for negative QBI is the 199A(c)(2) carryover, which the fix does not add. (6) The other part of the diff (the `deferred_outputs` block for 199A(c), (d), (h)) is module-level coverage bookkeeping: no rule in this module produces those outputs, so nothing became non-executable — unlike module 151 in the same squash. No PR reviews, no test-file change for 199A (199A.test.yaml sha256 unchanged in the manifest), and the commit/PR text never mentions floors or 199A.
